fields.h1: Build HOA Survey Questions That Reach Every Home
fields.hero_description: Get HOA survey questions for your community, sent to every homeowner, with one answer per home saved to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What Emergent Builds Into an HOA Survey
fields.features_subheading: Describe your community and the decision once, and Emergent builds the survey owners answer and the table behind it.
fields.feature_1:
Questions drafted for your community

Tell Emergent about the community and the decision the board faces, such as the pool budget. Emergent drafts questions to match, and a short prompt rewords or removes any of them.
fields.feature_2:
One answer for each home

Load the owner roster with lot or unit numbers. The survey asks for the unit first and keeps one answer per home, so a second reply from the same address replaces the first one.
fields.feature_3:
Emailed to the roster, with a reminder

The app emails every owner on the roster a link to the survey. Three days before it closes, homes that have not answered get one reminder, and homes that have answered hear nothing.
fields.feature_4:
Answers in a database the HOA owns

Each answer is a row in a database you own, tagged with the street or building it came from. The board can sort results by section and set this year's numbers beside next year's.
fields.feature_5:
Built for owners on their phones

Switch on one question per screen, and owners answer from the email link without zooming in or scrolling through a long form. A count at the top shows how many questions are left.
fields.feature_6:
On your domain, in GitHub on paid plans

Run the survey on the association's own domain, which is included in Emergent and uses credits. On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository and keep building.

fields.usecase_heading: Four HOA Surveys and What Changed
fields.tab_content_1:
Pool hours or a repaint? 58 homes rank the pool first

Ternwood Ridge sets its budget in November. In October, the board emails all 214 homeowners a survey ranking five amenity upgrades. By the close, 131 homes answered, and 58 of the 131 ranked longer pool hours first. The board funded the extra pool hours in the 2027 budget and moved the clubhouse repaint to 2028.
fields.tab_content_2:
Leaf pickup scores 2 or lower from 61 owners

Calloway Bluff's landscaping contract renews in March. In January, owners get an email survey rating mowing and leaf pickup on a 1 to 5 scale. If half rate a service 2 or lower, the community manager gets an email. Leaf pickup drew 61 low ratings out of 97. The renewed contract adds weekly leaf pickup each fall.
fields.tab_content_3:
Every new owner hears trash day on the first line

Thirty days after closing, every new owner at Dunmore Glen gets an email with 5 questions about settling in. One asks what they still could not find out. Across the last 11 new owners, 4 named the trash pickup day. The board's welcome email now opens with trash day, ahead of the pool and gate rules.
fields.tab_content_4:
One garage charger, and 47 of 70 units want it

Lockhaven Towers has 88 units and one parking garage. The board emailed each unit a phone survey, one question per screen, about adding a shared EV charger. Owners in 70 units replied, and 47 of the 70 said they would use the charger. The board asked two installers for quotes to show at the annual meeting.

fields.howto_title: How to Write HOA Survey Questions
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to write HOA survey questions that every home answers once, then build the survey with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Put the cost beside each option
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write down the decision the board has to make before you write a single question, such as which amenity gets next year's money. Any question whose answer cannot change that decision comes out of the survey.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Two owners at one address can disagree. Settle before launch who answers for the home. Put the lot or unit number first, and say in the intro that each home gets one answer.
fields.howto_step_3_des: When an option costs money, print the estimate next to it, such as $18,000 for a clubhouse repaint. A ranking without prices turns into a wish list the budget cannot cover.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Ask whether owners would use a garage charger, not whether they support finally modernizing the garage. Loaded words push answers one way, and a result a reworded question would flip is hard to defend.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Hold the survey to eight questions or fewer, with the decision question first. Owners open the email between other things, and anyone who stops early has still answered the one that matters.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Close the survey a week before the board meeting. That leaves time to read every comment and prepare the numbers. Put the dates in your prompt, and Emergent builds the send and close dates into the survey.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Share what the board will do
fields.howto_step_7_des: Publish the counts in the next newsletter or at the meeting, with one line on what the board will do next. Owners then see where their answers went before the next survey reaches them.

faq_plan.a: HOA survey questions are the questions a homeowners association board sends its owners before a decision, such as how to spend next year's amenity budget or whether to renew a vendor. A useful set ties every question to that decision and counts one answer per home.

faq_plan.q: How do I create hoa survey questions?
faq_plan.a: Start from the decision, then write one question for each fact the board needs to make it. With Emergent's AI survey builder, you describe the community and the decision in a prompt, and Emergent builds the survey, the owner email, and the table that stores each home's answer.

faq_plan.q: How many HOA survey questions should one survey include?
faq_plan.a: For one decision, a handful is enough: the decision question, a cost or tradeoff question, and an open comment box. An annual community survey can carry 15 to 20, grouped by topic, with each group short enough to finish on its own.

faq_plan.q: What rating scale works best for HOA survey questions?
faq_plan.a: A 1 to 5 scale labeled at both ends works well for rating services such as landscaping or pool upkeep. Keep the same scale every year; that lets the board set this year's ratings beside last year's. The habit carries across topics, and if you also write airline survey questions or any survey that repeats, fix the scale before the first round.

faq_plan.q: Should answers to HOA survey questions be anonymous?
faq_plan.a: It depends on the question. Ratings of a contractor or the management company get franker answers with names off, while a question that counts one answer per home needs the unit number. For those, record the unit and show the board only totals. Because the HOA owns the database behind the app Emergent builds, the board decides who opens the raw table.

faq_plan.q: How do I get more homeowners to answer HOA survey questions?
faq_plan.a: Tell owners in the first line which decision the answers feed and the date the board decides. Post the link where owners already look, such as the newsletter and the mailroom board, and share the response count halfway through. Emergent includes custom domains, which use credits, and a link on the association's web address reads as the HOA's own.

faq_plan.q: How should a board share answers to HOA survey questions with owners?
faq_plan.a: Share the totals for every question, not only the winning option, with the decision the board made and the reason for it. Present them at the next open meeting and in the newsletter. Afterward, a few post meeting survey questions can check whether owners understood what was decided.

faq_plan.q: Should renters answer HOA survey questions too?
faq_plan.a: Yes, when the question is about daily life in the community, such as pool hours or trash pickup, since they live with the result. Keep questions about dues and the budget to owners, and tag each answer as owner or renter so the board can read the two groups apart. Check your governing documents for any rule on who may be surveyed.

faq_plan.q: Which HOA survey questions rate a management company?
faq_plan.a: Ask how quickly the management company answers a request and whether problems get fixed on the first visit, each on the same rating scale. End with an open question about one thing the company should change. The app can also send each rating to the board's other tools through their API, ready for the next contract review.

faq_plan.q: Which HOA survey questions help recruit committee volunteers?
faq_plan.a: Ask which committee each volunteer wants to join and how many hours a month they can give. If the board plans training for new committee members, borrow from learning and development survey questions and ask which skills they want to build first.

plan.angle: The top 10 for hoa survey questions are buyer checklists (questions to ask before buying into an HOA), a law firm blog, forum threads and a property manager interview list; none shows a board surveying its own homeowners or what the answers changed. This page is for the board side: four HOA surveys built from a prompt and run to a decision, an amenity ranking before the budget, a landscaping review before a contract renewal, a 30-day check with new owners, and a garage EV charger survey in a condo building. The how-to gives the writing rules boards need (one answer per home, cost beside each option, a close date before the meeting), and the FAQ covers length, anonymity, renters, response rates and sharing results.
